![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081888/assets/41e7b3f6588f7f4dd55096fb95bbe517a053c11f80c43aab171d80829864d2c3.png)

The total area $A$ of the region between the curve $y=3x-2{x}^{2}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=1$ to $x=\sqrt{10}$ is given by the integral expression below. What is the value of $a?$

$$
A={\int }_{1}^{a}(3x-2{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{a}^{\sqrt{10}}(3x-2{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
To determine the missing limit of integration, we need to find the $x$-intercept of the curve $y=3x-2{x}^{2}.$ So, we set $y=0$ and solve for $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-2{x}^{2} & =0 \\ x(3-2x) & =0 \\ x & =0,\,\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\frac{3}{2}\in [1,4],$ we have two regions:

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=1$ to $x=\frac{3}{2}.$

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=\frac{3}{2}$ to $x=\sqrt{10}.$

So, $a=\frac{3}{2}$ and the final expression will be

$$
A={\int }_{1}^{3/2}(3x-2{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{3/2}^{\sqrt{10}}(3x-2{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.
$$
